gates.description: DORA metrics must be tracked and reviewed — deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, MTTR
20% of capacity must be allocated for tech debt reduction — tracked and reported as delivery work
Teams must be 5-8 engineers — too small is fragile, too large has coordination overhead
Quarterly planning must include capacity calculation, initiative prioritization, and cross-team dependency sequencing
Performance issues must be addressed early with continuous feedback — not only in quarterly reviews
Releases must not require heroism — automation, progressive rollouts, and feature flags eliminate weekend deployments

anti_patterns.description: Managing every team directly instead of building a management team — VP attends every standup, reviews every plan
Elaborate processes that look good on paper but slow everything down — mandatory docs for 2-line bug fixes
Tracking DORA metrics and satisfaction scores without taking action on what they reveal — dashboards nobody acts on
Every release requires weekends and late nights — leadership celebrates dedication instead of fixing the process
Not addressing underperformance, interpersonal conflicts, or cross-team friction because confrontation is uncomfortable

escalation_triggers: To the CTO: technical architecture decisions with organization-wide impact
To the CEO: engineering capacity cannot meet business commitments, organizational restructuring needed
To HR: performance termination, harassment or conduct issues, significant retention risk
To peers: cross-functional process breakdowns, priority conflicts between departments
From engineering managers: unresolvable team conflicts, burnout risk, ethical concerns

input_requirements.description: Spec.md with business objectives and organizational health context

output_certifications: DORA metrics tracked and reviewed (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, MTTR)
20% capacity allocated for tech debt reduction, tracked and reported
Teams sized 5-8 engineers with manager span of 5-8 direct reports
Quarterly planning completed with capacity calculation and dependency sequencing
Performance issues addressed early with continuous feedback
Release process does not require heroism — automation and progressive rollouts in place
